examTitle: Geography of Ethiopia and the Horn (GeES1011) Mid-Examination
department: Department of Geography and Environmental Studies
target: 1st Year Natural and Social Science Students

questions.question: Geography is a holistic and interdisciplinary field of study contributing to the understanding of the changing spatial structures from the past to the future.
questions.explanation: Geography integrates natural and social sciences to study spatial structures across time.

questions.question: The Rift Valley region of Ethiopia is the most stable part of the country.
questions.explanation: The Rift Valley is tectonically and seismically the most unstable and active zone in Ethiopia.

questions.question: The north central massif has the largest proportion of elevated ground from the western physiographic division.
questions.explanation: The North Central Massifs accommodate the majority of landmass above 3,000 meters in the western highlands.

questions.question: The Adigrat sandstone is older and thicker in the southeast and progressively decreases in age and thickness northwestward.
questions.explanation: Transgression of the Mesozoic sea began from the southeast, making southeastern deposits older and thicker.

questions.question: The ratio of area of country to its boundary length is higher then, the greater the degree of compactness.
questions.explanation: A higher area-to-perimeter (boundary length) ratio indicates a shape closer to a circle, hence more compact.

questions.question: Topographical maps are types of maps which used to show the distribution of temperature on the earth's surface.
questions.explanation: Topographical maps depict physical relief and surface features; maps showing temperature are climatic/thematic maps.

questions.question: The lower the Area-Circumference ratio, the smaller the degree of compactness.
questions.explanation: A lower Area-Circumference ratio represents greater elongation or irregularity and lower compactness.

questions.question: The scope of geography comprises only atmosphere and hydrosphere.
questions.explanation: The scope of geography spans all earth spheres: atmosphere, hydrosphere, lithosphere, and biosphere.

questions.question: The south-eastern lowlands of Ethiopia support few population as the area experiences harsh climatic condition.
questions.explanation: Arid to semi-arid conditions and high temperatures limit high population density in the south-eastern lowlands.

questions.question: During which geological era did the formation of the East African Great Rift Valley take place?
questions.explanation: Rifting and volcanism associated with the Great Rift Valley occurred predominantly during the Cenozoic (Tertiary and Quaternary).

questions.question: In which geological era was the major crystalline basement complex rock of Ethiopia formed?
questions.explanation: Precambrian rocks form the fundamental crystalline basement upon which younger strata rest.

questions.question: Fossil evidence on rock shows that marine life began in Ethiopia during which era?
questions.explanation: Mesozoic marine transgression brought abundant marine deposition and fossil-rich strata (e.g., Antalo limestone).

questions.question: Denudation and peneplanation of gigantic land forms in the Horn of Africa predominantly occurred during the:
questions.explanation: The Paleozoic was a long era of denudation, weathering, and peneplanation of the Precambrian relief.

questions.question: Sea transgression and regression across Ethiopia and the Horn occurred during the:
questions.explanation: The Mesozoic Era is characterized by the advance (transgression) and retreat (regression) of the Tethys / Indian Ocean sea.

questions.question: Prolonged folding and orogenetic processes in the Horn primarily shaped rocks of the:
questions.explanation: Orogenic mountain building and intense folding produced the metamorphic basement complex during the Precambrian.

questions.question: Major epeirogenesis (vertical continental uplifting) affecting Ethiopia's current relief structure occurred in the:
questions.explanation: Massive regional epeirogenic uplift of the Arabo-Ethiopian swell occurred during the Tertiary period of the Cenozoic.

questions.question: Due to longitudinal extension, Ethiopia has a time difference of one hour between the most easterly (Ogaden at 48°E) and most westerly (Akobo at 33°E) points. Assuming that a flight takes only one hour and the airplane departs from Ogaden at 8:00 AM local time, what will be the landing time of the airplane at Akobo in local Akobo time?
questions.explanation: Ogaden (48°E) is 1 hour ahead of Akobo (33°E). At 8:00 AM in Ogaden, it is 7:00 AM in Akobo. After a 1-hour flight, the local time at Akobo is 8:00 AM.

questions.question: Which of the following minerals is not found in Ethiopia?
questions.explanation: Gold, tantalum, and various base metals (iron, copper, zinc) are all documented mineral resources in Ethiopia.

questions.question: Which one of the following is not correct about the topography of Ethiopia?
options: Ethiopia has the largest proportion of elevated landmass in African continent
The altitudinal ranges of Ethiopia is small
More than 50% of the Ethiopian landmass is highland
Because of its height and large area, Ethiopia is the Roof of East Africa
questions.explanation: Ethiopia has an extremely large altitudinal range, spanning from 125m below sea level (Danakil Depression) up to 4,550m (Ras Dejen).

questions.question: Assume that the Boundary-Circumference ratio of Ethiopia, Somalia, Djibouti, and Eritrea is 1.5, 1.59, 1.8, and 1.23 respectively. Which country is the most compact?
questions.explanation: In Boundary-Circumference indices, a ratio closer to 1.0 reflects lower boundary deviation from a circular perimeter, indicating higher compactness.

questions.question: Which one of the following is a characteristic of the Ethiopian Highlands?
options: It is attractive for human habitation but the population densities is lower
The possibility of rain-fed agriculture is higher than irrigation agriculture
It is favorable for irrigation agriculture because of vast plain lands
There is higher amount of mean annual rainfall and temperature
questions.explanation: Ample orographic precipitation and temperate climate make rain-fed agriculture the predominant practice across the Ethiopian highlands.

questions.question: The Afar Triangle is characterized by all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Elevation uniformly drops towards north and east from south west
The Afar and Aisha horst separates the area from the main Ethiopian rift part
It is the widest and lowest part of the rift valley
An area where the Red Sea, the Gulf of Aden and the East African System meets
questions.explanation: All listed statements are true geographical characteristics of the Afar depression and its tectonic junction.

questions.question: Which one of the following is the largest physiographic subdivision in the western highlands of Ethiopia?
questions.explanation: The North Central Massifs (comprising Simien, Gonder, Wollo, and Gojjam massifs) form the largest unit in the western highlands.

questions.question: Which one of the following was used as evidence by Alfred Wegener to hypothesize continental drift?
options: Continental glaciations in India, Australia and South America
Match up of mountain belts in West Africa, North America, and Greenland
questions.explanation: Continental jigsaw fit, paleoclimatic glacial deposits, and matching structural mountain chains all served as evidence for continental drift.

questions.question: Which of the following typical features best characterizes the Bale Mountains of the southeastern highland?
options: The extensive exposed features of Mesozoic rocks
The Afro-Alpine summit of Senetti plateau
The prominent feature of the Jemjem plateau
Erosion features belonging to Pleistocene glaciation
questions.explanation: The Bale Mountains feature both the extensive high-altitude Afro-Alpine Sanetti Plateau and prominent glacial relict topography from the Pleistocene.

questions.question: What is the chronological deposition order of Mesozoic sedimentary rock layers in Ethiopia from oldest (bottom) to youngest (top)?
options: Upper Sandstone -> Antalo Limestone -> Adigrat Sandstone
Adigrat Sandstone -> Antalo Limestone -> Upper Sandstone
Antalo Limestone -> Adigrat Sandstone -> Upper Sandstone
Adigrat Sandstone -> Upper Sandstone -> Antalo Limestone
questions.explanation: Adigrat sandstone was deposited first during sea transgression, followed by Antalo limestone, and Upper sandstone formed during sea regression.

questions.question: Which physiographic sub-region contains the lowest point in Ethiopia?
questions.explanation: The Kobar Sink in the Danakil Depression drops to approximately 125 meters below sea level.

questions.question: The Main Ethiopian Rift (MER) connects which two tectonic systems?
options: The Afar Triple Junction and the Chew Bahir / Gregory Rift
The Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea
The Nile Valley and the Indian Ocean
The Congo Basin and the Mozambique Belt
questions.explanation: The Main Ethiopian Rift extends from the southern apex of the Afar depression down to the Lake Turkana / Chew Bahir rift basin.

questions.question: Which of the following highland peaks is the highest summit in Ethiopia?
questions.explanation: Ras Dejen in the Simien Mountains (North Central Massif) is the highest elevation in Ethiopia at 4,550 meters.

questions.question: Which geological period in the Cenozoic era was characterized by widespread volcanic trap series that capped the plateaus of Ethiopia?
questions.explanation: Extensive fissure eruptions during the Tertiary period formed the thick basaltic Trap Series across the Ethiopian plateau.
